chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) read to me the sheet of the Book of Inheritance shares, which is the dictation of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the handwriting of Ali (peace be upon him) with his own hand.

So I found in it: 'A man left a daughter and a mother; for the daughter is half, three shares, and for the mother is one-sixth, one share. The estate is divided into four shares; whatever amounts to three shares is for the daughter, and whatever amounts to one share is for the mother.'

He said: And I read in it: 'A man left a daughter and a father; for the daughter is half, three shares, and for the father is one-sixth, one share. The estate is divided into four shares; whatever amounts to three is for the daughter, and whatever amounts to one share is for the father.'

key_terms.إِمْلاَءُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Dictation of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: How is the estate divided when a man leaves a daughter and his parents?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the authority of the 'Sheet of Inheritance' (Sahifat al-Fara'id), attributed to the Prophet's dictation and Imam Ali's handwriting, as a primary source for Shia jurisprudence. It specifically addresses the scenario of a deceased leaving a daughter and parents, establishing the daughter's half share and the parents' one-sixth shares, which aligns with the Quranic verses but provides the detailed fractional breakdown (tawzi') often elaborated in Shia legal theory. This narration underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition through the Ahl al-Bayt in preserving precise inheritance calculations.
